newsitem.title: USA: US foreign crudes subdued ahead of industry event.
newsitem.headline: US foreign crudes subdued ahead of industry event.

text.p: The foreign crude scene on the U.S. Gulf Coast was subdued on Friday as buyers and sellers prepared for an annual industry event beginning Sunday evening, traders said.
The National Petroleum Refiners Association meeting is likely to keep activity at bay until it winds down on Tuesday.
Despite the mellow climate, the general sentiment on the Gulf Coast was that plenty of foreign barrels are still looking for a home.
Swiss-based Glencore threw the market into a tailspin the past two weeks by selling at least four North Sea Brent cargoes for early April arrival.
The last deal was heard at West Texas Intermediate/Cushing minus 80 cents a barrel.
Now the trading house is talking about bringing in more Brents for later in the month.
West African crude remains plentiful amid tepid demand in Europe and the Far East.
Bonny Light was assessed at the equivalent of dated Brent plus $1.60-75 a barrel delivered.
Brass River was pegged at dated Brent plus $1.70.
Elsewhere, state Petroecuador lifted its force majeure declaration on March Oriente cargoes effective Friday.
Only some eight to 10 cargoes are expected to be affected.
The loading dates have been pushed forward by a a few days as a result of the measure.
Petroecuador declared force majeure after a pump on the main Transecuadoran pipeline exploded on March 7. Pumping operations were back to normal on March 12.
From Colombia, Cusiana was assessed at WTI minus $1.00 a barrel, trade sources said.
Cano Limon was on offer at around WTI minus $2.75 a barrel for third decade March loading, while Vasconia was being shown at WTI minus $3.30 for end-March loading.
